claims.statement: GDPR treats health data as a special category whose processing is prohibited unless a specified exception applies, including explicit consent for specified purposes where legally available.
The EHDS establishes governed secondary-use pathways and expressly preserves contractual or administrative access arrangements, while imposing permitted-purpose and secure-processing constraints.

contrary_evidence: Explicit consent is not a blanket commercialization right; withdrawal, power imbalance, national law, medical secrecy, and EHDS rules can restrict or end use.

economics.acquisition_route: Dental software resellers, imaging-equipment distributors, and clinic groups distribute a standardized consent-and-governance package
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Enroll 40 clinics by year 3 (unvalidated), create a multicountry governed network by year 7 (unvalidated), and reach founder equity above PLN 5 million by year 9 (unvalidated)
economics.founder_time: 15-22 hours per week during validation (unvalidated), with legal, privacy, and clinical officers retained
economics.gross_margin_basis: Secure compute, governance review, and curation dominate cost; 45-65% gross margin (unvalidated)
economics.pricing: PLN 3000-8000 clinic membership per year (unvalidated) and PLN 50000-200000 per approved research access project (unvalidated)
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual clinic membership (unvalidated) and repeated longitudinal follow-up studies

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal outcome linkage, consent lineage, and multi-clinic coverage cannot be reconstructed from public image sets
fingerprint.customer: Independent dental clinics, dental-imaging and device developers, universities, and clinical researchers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Dental software and imaging-equipment channel partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Consent operations, pseudonymized longitudinal linkage, clinic benchmarks, and controlled research workspaces
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Clinic pays for governance and benchmarks; researcher pays only after a study is approved for secure access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A clinic wants outcome benchmarking or a developer needs lawful longitudinal validation evidence

founder_fit: Strong match to health, AI, and data-science interests.
Requires expert legal and clinical partners beyond the founder's own competence.
risks: High compliance, cybersecurity, and reputational burden.
Research buyers may prefer public or hospital datasets.
The stated PLN 190000 startup capital requirement is unvalidated.

structure.commercial_archetype: Governed research-access cooperative for consented longitudinal health evidence
structure.control_point: Purpose-bound consent records plus longitudinal image-outcome linkage across independent clinics
structure.critical_dependency: GDPR, medical confidentiality, EHDS transition, consent withdrawal, ethics, security, and downstream medical-device obligations must all be satisfied

thesis: Form a clinic-governed network that obtains explicit, purpose-specific patient permission for longitudinal dental images and outcomes, pseudonymizes them, and allows only approved secure-environment analyses. Clinics receive quality and follow-up benchmarks; medtech researchers pay for governed study access rather than receiving raw patient files. No data is acquired or reused without documented legal basis and clinical governance.
title: Dental Evidence Vault
uncertainties: Whether clinics will act as joint governors and support follow-up labeling.
Which access model remains workable through EHDS implementation in Poland?
